significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that an "InterferenceLoad" defined by the "#competitors weighted by cosine proximity" predictively couples representational crowding to single-example recall failure, and that high-proximity competitors causally intrude because suppressing their direction restores the correct token. This is chiefly a form-(iii) predictive relation combined with a form-(ii) mechanism: it fixes expected failure rankings and explanations for known-but-wrong answers, extending the staged factual-recall picture analyzed by Geva et al. (2023) into a concrete account of one failure source. The phenomenon is competitor-shaped factual errors and the mechanism is directional interference; a negative result would distinguishably rule out crowding as a general explanation and favor generic difficulty, missing knowledge, or retrieval noise, although it would not by itself choose among those alternatives. In the topic-substitution check, deleting the competitor-load relation and causal-intrusion mechanism leaves only the generic question of why stored knowledge fails to influence answers, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The named handles are the measurable "InterferenceLoad" predictor and the "competitor-aware retrieval nudge" that subtracts an interfering direction. The predictor is ex ante because it forecasts "whether retrieval of the correct fact will succeed or fail" before the answer is finalized, while the nudge supplies an inference-time action window; these could support auditing, gating, or runtime correction rather than only post-hoc analysis. Although directions require re-extraction, the substantive relation—greater competitor count/proximity predicts failure and identifies the likely intrusion—would still predict what to find after recalibration across the asserted class of factual-retrieval tasks, while the architecture-specific caveat limits any stronger universality claim. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this reach: the broad topic alone supplies neither an advance-warning quantity nor an intervention usable by model auditors or deployers.
